authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 6984 nava “nine” lists eastern na, northern nau/nao and western nao/nau. The survey numeral meanings distinguish them from the nava “new” homonym despite similar forms. The comparative family link retains uncertainty about transfer between Indo-Aryan languages.

assignments.Notes: CDIAL 6984 nava “nine” lists eastern na, northern nau/nao and western nao/nau. The survey numeral meanings distinguish them from the nava “new” homonym despite similar forms. The comparative family link retains uncertainty about transfer between Indo-Aryan languages. Joint SIL review 2026-09-14.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 6658.1 dvādaśa gives northern bāra/bāh and eastern bāra “twelve”. It explicitly separates Torwali/Maiya duāš under 6658.2 duvādaśa; those survey forms are assigned to the latter node. The comparative family link retains uncertainty about transfer between Indo-Aryan languages.
